key_insight: General-purpose LLMs outperform the tested domain-specific pretrained models for alloy property prediction, with further gains when guided by numerical predictions from a prior model.
engineering_relevance: Combining general-purpose LLMs with existing predictors and carefully selected reference data could reduce reliance on costly materials-specific pretraining.
method: Benchmark general-purpose LLMs against SteelBERT, MatSciBERT, and SciBERT across Ti, steel, high-entropy, and Al alloys.
Prompt DeepSeek V3.1 and Gemini-2.5-Flash with CatBoost or SteelBERT estimates to refine predictions.
Assess reference-data similarity, data quantity, and self-reported prediction confidence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that using only the highest-similarity 5% of training data as references achieves performance similar to using the full training set, while high self-reported confidence correlates with smaller prediction errors.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical error metrics or split details, limiting assessment of effect sizes and robustness under distribution shift.
paper_title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction
